known_before_registration: boundary-shift-novelty-null (PR #34): boundary-shift alone is provably H1/H2-invariant but structurally capped near 63.8% hapax even at maximum dosage (nu=1.0) -- confirmed a hard supply ceiling, and confirmed multi-pass re-scanning does not raise it (shifted pieces are unseen by construction so essentially never recur to create new eligibility)

bigram-novelty-null (PR #30): bigram-conditional character substitution easily clears the hapax floor (70%+ at nu=0.2) but costs H2; at LOW dosage (nu=0.1, a non-primary sensitivity) it costs much less H2 and passed in a majority of seeds

hypothesis under test, not yet verified: applying boundary-shift first (to absorb as much hapax gain as its free capacity allows) and using character substitution only as a small top-up for the remaining gap might combine most of shift's zero-entropy-cost vocabulary growth with only a sliver of substitution's H2 cost
not_done_before_registration: No hybrid stream generated or scored
No parameter selected from any transformed outcome
nu_sub calibration (self-consistency-only, hapax-only) not yet run -- nu_shift is fixed at 1.0 (boundary-shift's own maximum capacity, already established, not re-tested as a free variable)

claim: Applying boundary-shift at its maximum capacity (nu_shift=1.0) first, then a small amount of bigram-conditional character substitution (nu_sub, calibrated to the smallest value that closes the remaining hapax gap) as a top-up on tokens still repeated afterward, passes all six frozen criteria in at least 16 of 20 primary replicates.
honesty_precommitment: If this hybrid does not clear the manipulation checks, or does not improve on both prior designs simultaneously, that will be reported plainly. This is not a guaranteed win: it is possible the small substitution top-up still costs enough H2 to fail, or that combining the two operations reintroduces the order-share problem in a way neither did alone, or interacts with boundary-shift's own manipulation-check failure in a way that still invalidates the design.
base_mechanism: Naibbe cipher (voynich-units commit 956a7c4fc39981f4d116fa3f4edfccce6d065571) + identical boundary-coupling rule (beta=0.50 fixed, unchanged from every prior design).

representation.roundtrip_required: collapse(expand(atom)) == atom for every atomic_alphabet symbol

boundary_shift_at_max_capacity.note: identical mechanics to boundary-shift-novelty-null, run at its own established maximum (nu_shift is not re-tested as a free variable here -- its ceiling is already established)

bigram_substitution_topup.eligibility: token is still a repeat of something already emitted AFTER the boundary-shift pass has run (i.e., a repeat that boundary-shift did not or could not resolve into novel pieces -- most commonly because it was consumed as the RIGHT member of a shift pair rather than being eligible as a LEFT member, or because no shift fired for it)
bigram_substitution_topup.mechanism: identical single-atom bigram-conditional exhaustive substitution search used in bigram-novelty-null (same statistic, same sparse-context fallback, same cold-start rule, same protected position 0)
bigram_substitution_topup.note: this pass operates on the boundary-shift pass's OUTPUT stream, scanning left to right exactly as bigram-novelty-null does, with its own independent running bigram/unigram frequency tables built fresh over this pass (not shared with any statistics internal to the shift pass, which tracks no character frequency at all)

baseline.note: identical to boundary-state-null's baseline; not rerun, reused by reference

edge_only.note: identical to boundary-state-null's edge_only; not rerun, reused by reference

shift_only_no_topup.note: isolates how much of the primary's hapax comes from shift alone at this beta, for interpretation

configurations.pilot_calibration_rule: nu_sub chosen by a self-consistency-only pilot (3 seeds, hybrid_novelty_only config, beta=0, nu_shift=1.0 fixed) targeting hapax_share_of_types in [0.65, 0.75], selecting the SMALLEST nu_sub that lands in-band. Swept {0.01,0.02,0.03,0.05,0.08,0.1}: 0.01 undershoots (0.6467), 0.02 is the smallest in-band value (0.6543). Frozen: nu_sub=0.02, chosen on hapax alone -- H1/H2/order were recorded during the pilot (H2 mean 2.735, order mean 0.0220 at nu_sub=0.02) but explicitly NOT used to select nu_sub, even though a slightly higher nu_sub looked more favorable on order in the pilot data. Picking nu_sub post-hoc to make order look better would be exactly the kind of outcome-driven parameter selection this project's discipline forbids. Full pilot log in logs/2026-09-21-claude-hybrid-shift-substitution-selfreview.md.

boundary.note: reused from boundary-state-null's edge_only vs baseline comparison, not recomputed

novelty.note: checked against hybrid_novelty_only (shift+topup together, no coupling) vs baseline -- this is the FULL novelty mechanism for this design, not decomposed further into shift-alone and topup-alone components, since the hybrid is being tested as one combined operation, not as two independently-valid ones (shift alone is already known to fail its own isolated check, per PR #34 -- this design does not re-litigate that, it builds on top of it deliberately)

primary_verdict.pass: Both manipulation checks succeed and at least 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria
primary_verdict.fail: Both manipulation checks succeed and fewer than 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria

execution_embargo: Do not implement the transformation beyond the pilot-calibration step, or calculate any primary/control/sensitivity outcome, until the self-review pass documented in the accompanying log is complete.
